 Reliance Industries shares surged nearly 12% after record Q2 earnings, emerging as the top Nifty gainer, biggest index contributor and most active stock on NSE and BSE. Goldman Sachs and Nomura retained Buy ratings. 
 Shaleen Agrawal 
 November 02, 2026 / 15:35 IST Share -->

 Consolidated revenue hit an all-time high of Rs 3.62 lakh crore.
 Brokerages maintained Buy ratings with bullish target prices.

 Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) shares surged nearly 12 percent in on Monday, following the company's record Q2 FY27 earnings and bullish outlook from brokerages. The stock emerged as the top gainer and the biggest positive contributor to the Nifty 50 index, while also becoming the most actively traded stock on both the NSE and BSE.
 Reliance Industries shares ended at Rs 1,300, up 11.6 percent. The Mukesh Ambani-led conglomerate's market capitalisation stood at Rs 17.59 lakh crore. The rally in Reliance shares drove a broader market surge. At the end of the day, the Sensex was up 1,233 points, or 1.7 percent, at 75,693, while the Nifty gained 388 points to close at 23,441.
 Reliance Industries Q2 results: Record profit, revenue and EBITDA
 Reliance Industries reported its strongest-ever quarterly financial performance for the July-September quarter (Q2 FY27), with record revenue, EBITDA and net profit, driven by robust growth in its oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business, digital services and retail operations. Consolidated revenue surged 28 percent year-on-year to an all-time high of Rs 3.62 lakh crore, while EBITDA increased 24 percent to a record Rs 62,409 crore. Net profit jumped 34 percent to Rs 29,550 crore, also a quarterly record.

 The O2C business delivered its strongest-ever quarterly performance, with revenue rising 44.2 percent year-on-year to Rs 2.32 lakh crore and EBITDA surging 67.9 percent to Rs 25,203 crore. Transportation fuel cracks, a measure of refining margins, rose 3 to 3.7 times from a year earlier, reaching historic highs during the quarter.

 Reliance's digital services business also recorded growth, with Jio Platforms reporting an 11.3 percent year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 47,485 crore. Its EBITDA rose 16.6 percent to Rs 21,879 crore, supported by subscriber additions, higher average revenue per user and expansion in digital services.
 Brokerages bullish on Reliance Industries stock
 Goldman Sachs and Nomura maintained their Buy ratings on Reliance Industries following the company's record quarterly performance, citing strong refining earnings and steady growth in telecom, even as retail performance remained relatively weak. Goldman Sachs assigned a target price of Rs 1,840 per share, implying 58 percent upside from Friday's closing price of Rs 1,164.90.
 The brokerage said Reliance's Q2 EBITDA beat its estimates by 9 percent, led by strong O2C performance. However, it expects refining margins to moderate in the December quarter due to higher very large crude carrier (VLCC) freight costs, partly offset by processing discounted heavy crude.
 Nomura also retained its Buy rating, with a target price of Rs 1,560 per share. The brokerage attributed Reliance's record earnings to multi-decade-high refining cracks and noted that consolidated EBITDA rose 19 percent sequentially, beating estimates by 9 percent. Both brokerages highlighted steady growth in telecom, while pointing to weakness in Reliance Retail due to the shift in festive demand and investments in digital commerce.
